steps.say: A prism has two matching ends joined by rectangles. This is a triangular prism.

figure.alt: A picture of a triangular prism.

steps.say: A pyramid has one base and triangle faces that meet at a point.

figure.alt: A picture of a square-based pyramid.

steps.say: A net is a flat shape that folds up to make a 3D shape.

figure.alt: A net of 6 squares: a column of 4, with one square on each side of the second square.

steps.say: This net has 6 squares that fold into a cube without overlapping.
Not every set of 6 squares is a net. Folding 2 rows of 3 makes squares overlap.

check.prompt: A net has 2 triangles and 3 rectangles. Which 3D shape does it make?

options.why: Its net has 1 square and 4 triangles.
Its net has 2 circles and 1 rectangle.

hints: Each flat shape becomes one face.
Two matching ends joined by rectangles make a prism.
Look at the shape of the two ends.
check.explanation: The 2 triangles are the ends, and the 3 rectangles join them. That makes a triangular prism.

check.prompt: How many edges does a triangular prism have?
hints: Count the edges on each triangle end.
Then count the edges that join the two ends.
check.explanation: 3 edges on each end and 3 edges joining them. 3 + 3 + 3 = 9 edges.

figure.alt: A picture of a triangular prism.
